messages:
olivia: heads-up — started seeing p95/p99 regressions on /v1/generate in prod-eu at ~02:40 UTC. p95 climbed from ~180ms to ~650ms; p99 nearing 1.4s. Looks correlated with the batcher config change deployed 02:37 (rev: f9c12b).
raj: can you share the dashboard panels and which metrics? service-level or internal batcher wait?
olivia: service.request_latency.p95/p99 and batcher.wait_time_ms hist. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ai/batcher-overview?from=now-2h&panelId=8
maria: that was my change — bumped max_batch_wait_ms from 10 -> 55 and enabled adaptive_wait to improve throughput for some heavy-embedding flows. intended effect: fewer tiny batches.
kevin: that tradeoff can worsen tail for interactive routes. Increasing wait lets lonely requests sit until timeout; in bursty traffic that hurts p99.
olivia: we have a bursty client this morning and many mid-size prompts; requests that would have been singletons are now waiting the full 55ms and show up in the p99 bucket.
support-bot: Customer Escalation: #13077 8: acme-inc reported sluggish agent responses in EU region.
emma: customer reported slow interactive responses starting ~02:42 UTC. sample ids: req_e1a, req_e1b.
raj: repro plan: mimic customer traffic with Poisson bursts at ~35 RPS and the same prompt length distribution; compare histograms with max_batch_wait_ms=55 vs 10.
olivia: repro harness I used (docker):
```
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  seq 1 100 | xargs -n1 -P10 -I{} curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.prod/v1/generate > /dev/null
  sleep $((RANDOM%4))
done
```
kevin: share the exact config in prod.
maria: prod excerpt below:
```
batcher:
  max_batch_size: 64
  max_batch_wait_ms: 55  # previously 10
  min_batch_fill: 0.25
  adaptive_wait: true
  dynamic_timeout_ms: 18
```
david: logs from frontend (02:41-02:46):
```
I02041 02:42:12.430 batcher.cpp:398] created batch size=1 wait_ms=54
I02041 02:42:12.433 request_handler.cpp:101] serve req req_e1a latency=720ms
I02041 02:42:12.512 batcher.cpp:465] batch execute start idx=3 size=8
```
kevin: confirming: some batches with size=1 waited nearly full window. that's the tail source.
raj: mitigation options: immediate rollback to 10ms; or set max_batch_wait_ms=20 as intermediate; or route-level overrides to exclude interactive routes from adaptive wait.
olivia: customer SLA impact unacceptable; recommend quick rollback to 10ms, canary first 5% of pods in eu cluster.
david: recommend scripted rollback steps, canary via k8s env patch. sample commands I will run:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/llm-batcher BATCHER_MAX_WAIT_MS=10
kubectl rollout restart deploy/llm-batcher -n inference --grace-period=30
kubectl rollout status deploy/llm-batcher -n inference
```
raj: starting canary now (02:53 UTC) on node-pool canary-batcher-eu-1. monitor panels: service.p95, batcher.wait_time_ms{pod=llm-batcher-*}, request.latency.hist.
maria: i pushed a branch with route-labels for batcher tuning: feature/route-batcher (PR #462). We can set interactive routes to use tiny-wait policy.
kevin: long-term suggestions: 1) implement route-level configs, 2) autoscaler aware of batcher queue length, 3) safeguard that caps max effective wait under certain queue conditions.
olivia: customer comms: propose short message: "We identified a batching configuration change as root cause for increased latency and have initiated a rollback; you should see improvements shortly. We'll follow up with permanent fixes." ok to send?
emma: customer updated at 03:03 UTC; says slight improvements observed.
david: canary metrics at 03:05 UTC show canary pod p95 dropped from 650ms -> 200ms. good sign.
raj: rolling out full rollback to eu after canary verification. will perform staged rollouts with 2m pause between 20% increments.
olivia: after rollback, run the synthetic workload and post the histograms here. also capture per-route latency so we can quantify throughput loss for embedding routes.
maria: local experiments: when wait=55ms throughput improved ~12% for embedding-like flows but interactive p99 worsened ~3x. setting wait ~20ms kept most throughput benefits while reducing tail impact.
kevin: short-term compromise: set max_batch_wait_ms=20 and increase min_batch_fill to 0.6 for routes labeled interactive. that should favor responsiveness while keeping throughput for batch-heavy routes.
support-bot: Customer Escalation #13077 updated: action=rollback started, ETA=10m.
raj: full eu rollback completed at 03:11 UTC. immediate telemetry: service.p95 EU fell to ~210ms, p99 ~320ms, throughput dip ~7% vs 55ms config.
olivia: customer reported noticeable improvement ~5-8 minutes after rollback. I'll mark escalation as resolved pending 1h stability.
david: follow-ups/tickets:
- RB-701: route-level batcher config implementation + default profiles
- RB-702: rollback playbook for inference config changes (canary steps)
- RB-703: workload-aware load testing harness for bursty interactive patterns
maria: i'll author RFC on conservative defaults and a required canary/load test checklist for batcher tweak PRs.
kevin: add automated guard: if batcher.wait_time_ms p95 crosses threshold for >30s, trigger auto-reduce of max_wait_ms for affected route(s).
olivia: thanks team. I'll send a short update to customer and close escalate once monitors stable for 1h. closing notes: prefer smaller incremental increases to wait, always canary, and include route labeling in change PRs.
support-bot: Customer Escalation #13077 closed by olivia. resolution: rollback of batcher.wait config; follow-ups created.
